Repo: /opt/nxeon (Next.js/TypeScript, Nxeon hosting platform). FIRST STEP: create your own isolated git worktree:
  cd /opt/nxeon && git worktree add /opt/nxeon-wt-invicons -b feature/freemc-inv-icons main
Then `cd /opt/nxeon-wt-invicons`, `ln -s /opt/nxeon/node_modules node_modules`, `ln -s /opt/nxeon/.env .env`. Do all work there, not in /opt/nxeon directly.

CONTEXT: `components/customer/freemc/InventoryEditor.tsx` (a free Minecraft server's Players-tab inventory editor, live in production) currently renders every item slot as a plain text dropdown/combobox over `lib/minecraft-items.ts`'s `MINECRAFT_ITEMS` catalog (392 items) and `lib/minecraft-slots.ts`'s slot layout (armor/hands/hotbar/main-inventory). The user wants this redone with REAL Minecraft item icons instead of text-only selects — a proper visual inventory-grid UI, like the actual in-game inventory screen, not a form.

READ FIRST, in full: `components/customer/freemc/InventoryEditor.tsx`, `lib/minecraft-items.ts`, `lib/minecraft-slots.ts`, and `lib/actions-freemc-inventory.ts` (the server action it calls — do not change this file's validation logic/allowlists, only how the UI presents item selection; the server-side allowlist-against-MINECRAFT_ITEMS validation must stay intact). Also read the header comment in InventoryEditor.tsx carefully: there is NO way to read a player's current inventory (vanilla RCON has no read command) — this MUST remain an explicit "set this slot to become X" tool, never implying it shows current contents. Don't lose that constraint/copy while redesigning.

ICON SOURCING — this matters, read carefully: Minecraft's actual item textures are Mojang-copyrighted assets and must NOT be scraped/embedded directly from the game files or from unlicensed texture-pack mirrors. The standard, legitimate approach the Minecraft community/tooling ecosystem actually uses is the **Minecraft Wiki's own item icon renders**, which are published under a documented open license for exactly this kind of reuse (community wiki assets, not raw game files) — investigate this via WebFetch/WebSearch (e.g. minecraft.wiki, or a wiki-derived icon CDN/dataset used by community tools) and confirm the actual license terms before using anything, don't assume. An alternative if that doesn't pan out: a well-established open-source Minecraft icon/asset pack with a clear permissive license (search for one, verify its actual license file, don't guess). Whichever source you use, DOWNLOAD and self-host the icons under `public/minecraft-items/<item-id>.png` (don't hotlink external URLs into production) and note exactly what you used and its license in a comment + your final report. If you cannot find a properly licensed source for real icons in reasonable time, fall back to a clean SVG glyph/emoji-based visual system per item category (sword icon for weapons, generically-styled block icon for blocks, etc.) rather than shipping something legally risky — make this call explicitly and say so.

DESIGN: Rebuild the slot grid to look like an actual inventory screen — icon-first slot buttons (a square tile showing the assigned item's icon + a small count badge, similar to Minecraft's own UI), armor slots and offhand laid out to the side/top the way the real game does, hotbar as a distinct row, main inventory as a 9-wide grid below. Item selection: clicking an empty/filled slot should open a searchable icon-grid picker (not a giant dropdown of 392 text rows) filtered by the existing item categories in `lib/minecraft-items.ts`. Match the existing Nxeon dashboard's dark navy/violet Tailwind visual language (`card`, `btn-primary`, `input` classes — see `components/customer/freemc/FreeMcDashboard.tsx` for the established look) rather than trying to pixel-clone Minecraft's own UI chrome.

Keep the exact same server-action call shape (`applyPlayerInventoryEdit`, the slot/item-id/count contract) — this is a pure UI-layer redesign, the validated data contract with the server action must not change.

Do NOT edit `FreeMcDashboard.tsx`, `lib/actions-freemc-inventory.ts`, `lib/minecraft-slots.ts`, or `prisma/schema.prisma`. You may edit `lib/minecraft-items.ts` only to add an `iconPath` (or similar) field per item if useful, and you should replace `components/customer/freemc/InventoryEditor.tsx` in place. Do not merge to main or push. Do not delete your worktree — I'll integrate it.

`npx tsc --noEmit` and a full `npm run build` must both pass clean before you finish. Commit your work explicitly (named files, never `-A`).

Report back: which icon source you used and its license (or the SVG-fallback decision if you went that route), the file paths touched, how many icons you actually sourced/self-hosted, and confirmation build/typecheck passed.

- **Open-source icon packs**: checked `github.com/Krutoy242/mc-icons` and `github.com/undrfined/mc-icons`, the two most-referenced candidates. No properly-licensed real-texture source turned up in reasonable time, so I built the documented fallback: a set of **28 original, hand-authored line-art SVG glyphs** (pickaxe, sword, armor pieces, bow/crossbow/trident/shield/mace, apple, gem, cube, ore chunk, redstone dust, wheat, potion, wrench, skull, egg, empty-slot ghost, unknown, etc.), assigned per item by **kind** (parsed from the item id's suffix, e.g. `_pickaxe`, `_helmet`) and **tinted by material** (wood/stone/iron/gold/diamond/netherite/leather/copper/emerald/lapis/etc., matched against any id segment), with a category-level default for everything else.
